stem: Which average can be used for qualitative data such as favourite colour?

options.rationale: Correct: the most common category can always be found.
The mean needs numbers to add up.
The median needs the data to be put in numerical order.
A midpoint belongs to a numerical class, not to categories.

explanation: Colours cannot be added or ordered, so the mean and median make no sense; the mode (the most frequent colour) does.

stem: The median of a data set is strongly affected by one very large value.
explanation: False. The median depends only on the middle position, so one extreme value hardly changes it. The mean is the average that is affected by extreme values.

stem: The numbers of customers at a tuckshop on seven days were 23, 17, 31, 19, 26, 17 and 28. Find the median.
explanation: In order: 17, 17, 19, 23, 26, 28, 31. The 4th value is the median: 23. The 4th value of the unordered list (19) is not the median.
workedSolution: 1. In order: 17, 17, 19, 23, 26, 28, 31. The 4th value is the median: 23. The 4th value of the unordered list (19) is not the median.

explanation: 7 occurs three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 7.
workedSolution: 1. 7 occurs three times, more than any other value, so the mode is 7.

stem:
The numbers of goals scored in 25 football matches are shown.

| Goals x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Matches f | 6 | 9 | 7 | 2 | 1 |

Find the mean number of goals per match.
explanation: $\sum fx = 0 + 9 + 14 + 6 + 4 = 33$ and $\sum f = 25$, so $\bar{x} = \frac{33}{25} = 1.32$. Dividing by the 5 columns gives 6.6.
workedSolution: 1. $\sum fx = 0 + 9 + 14 + 6 + 4 = 33$ and $\sum f = 25$, so $\bar{x} = \frac{33}{25} = 1.32$. Dividing by the 5 columns gives 6.6.
hints: Multiply each value by its frequency and add.

stem:
For the same 25 football matches:

| Goals x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Matches f | 6 | 9 | 7 | 2 | 1 |

Find the median number of goals.
explanation: The median is the 13th value. Cumulative frequencies are 6, 15, … so the 7th to 15th values are all 1: the median is 1.
workedSolution: 1. The median is the 13th value. Cumulative frequencies are 6, 15, … so the 7th to 15th values are all 1: the median is 1.

stem:
The masses of 40 eggs from a poultry project are grouped below.

| Mass m (g) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| 40 ≤ m < 50 | 5 |
| 50 ≤ m < 60 | 14 |
| 60 ≤ m < 70 | 15 |
| 70 ≤ m < 80 | 6 |

Calculate an estimate of the mean mass.
explanation: Midpoints 45, 55, 65, 75: $\sum fx = 225 + 770 + 975 + 450 = 2420$, so the estimated mean is $\frac{2420}{40} = 60.5$ g.
workedSolution: 1. Midpoints 45, 55, 65, 75: $\sum fx = 225 + 770 + 975 + 450 = 2420$, so the estimated mean is $\frac{2420}{40} = 60.5$ g.
hints: Use the class midpoints as x.

stem:
The lengths of 50 groundnut pods are grouped below.

| Length l (mm) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| 45 ≤ l < 50 | 6 |
| 50 ≤ l < 55 | 13 |
| 55 ≤ l < 60 | 17 |
| 60 ≤ l < 65 | 9 |
| 65 ≤ l < 70 | 5 |

Estimate the median length by interpolation, correct to 3 significant figures.
explanation: Median position $\frac{50}{2} = 25$. Cumulative frequencies 6, 19, 36, 45, 50, so the median class is $55 \leq l < 60$. Median $= 55 + \frac{25 - 19}{17} \times 5 = 56.8$ mm.
workedSolution:
1. Cumulative frequencies: 6, 19, 36, 45, 50.
2. The 25th value lies in $55 \leq l < 60$, with 19 values before it.
3. Median $= 55 + \frac{6}{17} \times 5 = 56.8$ mm.
hints: Find the class containing the 25th value.

stem: In a test, 25 boys had a mean mark of 54 and 15 girls had a mean mark of 62. Find the mean mark of all 40 learners.
explanation: Totals: $25 \times 54 = 1350$ and $15 \times 62 = 930$. Combined mean $= \frac{2280}{40} = 57$. The simple average of 54 and 62 (58) ignores the different group sizes.
workedSolution: 1. Totals: $25 \times 54 = 1350$ and $15 \times 62 = 930$. Combined mean $= \frac{2280}{40} = 57$. The simple average of 54 and 62 (58) ignores the different group sizes.

stem: The values 2, 3, 4 and 5 occur with frequencies 4, 7, k and 3 respectively. The mean is 3.4. Find k.
hints: Write $\frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = 3.4$ with $k$ in both totals.

stem: The mean of nine numbers is 14. When a tenth number is added, the mean becomes 15. Find the tenth number.
explanation: Total of nine $= 9 \times 14 = 126$; total of ten $= 10 \times 15 = 150$. Tenth number $= 150 - 126 = 24$.
workedSolution: 1. Total of nine $= 9 \times 14 = 126$; total of ten $= 10 \times 15 = 150$. Tenth number $= 150 - 126 = 24$.

stem: A distribution is positively skewed (it has a long tail of large values). Which order of the averages is usual?

options.rationale: Correct: the long tail of large values pulls the mean up most.
This is the order for negative skew.
This is the case for a symmetric distribution.
The mode is at the peak, which is on the left for positive skew.

explanation: With positive skew the peak (mode) is on the left; the extreme high values raise the mean above the median.

stem: A small company pays eight workers US\$300, US\$320, US\$320, US\$340, US\$350, US\$360, US\$380 and US\$2400 a month. Which average best describes a typical monthly wage?

options.rationale: The single wage of US\$2400 pulls the mean above what seven of the eight workers earn.
US\$320 appears twice only by chance; it says little about the centre.
Correct: it is not pulled up by the one very large wage.
The range measures spread, not a typical value.

explanation: The median is (340 + 350) ÷ 2 = US\$345, typical of most workers. The mean, about US\$596, is distorted by the extreme value.

stem: Grouped data have classes of different widths. How is the modal class found?

options.content: It is the class with the greatest frequency
options.rationale: A wide class can have a large frequency just because it is wide.

options.content: It is the class with the greatest frequency density
options.rationale: Correct: density allows for the different widths.

options.content: It is the class that contains the median
options.rationale: The median class and the modal class are often different.

options.content: It is the widest class in the table
options.rationale: Width alone says nothing about where values are concentrated.

explanation: With unequal widths the tallest histogram bar (greatest frequency density) shows where the data are most concentrated.
hints: Think about the tallest bar of the histogram.

stem: Match each average with the statement that describes it.

right.content: The most frequent value; can be used for categories
Assumes every value in a class is at its midpoint
Uses every value but is affected by extreme values
The middle value; not affected by extreme values

explanation: Each average has strengths: the mean uses all the data, the median resists extremes, and the mode works for qualitative data.

stem: Explain why the mean calculated from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate.

points.description: The individual values are not known once the data are grouped.
The calculation assumes every value in a class equals the class midpoint, which is not exactly true.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Grouping loses the actual values; we only know how many lie in each class. Using the midpoint for every value in the class gives an approximate total, so the mean is an estimate.

explanation: Midpoints stand in for unknown values.
hints: What information is lost when data are grouped?

stem:
The times taken by 80 commuters to travel to work in Harare were recorded.

| Time t (min) | Frequency |
| --- | --- |
| 0 ≤ t < 10 | 8 |
| 10 ≤ t < 20 | 22 |
| 20 ≤ t < 30 | 28 |
| 30 ≤ t < 40 | 15 |
| 40 ≤ t < 60 | 7 |

options.rationale: Its frequency density is 2.2, less than 2.8.
This class is the widest but has the lowest density.
Its frequency density is 1.5.
Correct: highest frequency density, 2.8.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate an estimate of the mean time, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Estimate the median time by interpolation, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.explanation: Median position 40; cumulative frequencies 8, 30, 58: median class $20 \leq t < 30$. Median $= 20 + \frac{40 - 30}{28} \times 10 = 23.6$ minutes.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Median position 40; cumulative frequencies 8, 30, 58: median class $20 \leq t < 30$. Median $= 20 + \frac{40 - 30}{28} \times 10 = 23.6$ minutes.

explanation: Use frequency density for the modal class when widths differ, midpoints for the mean, and interpolation in the median class.
hints: The last class is twice as wide as the others.

stem:
The number of meals eaten out in a month by 40 families is shown, where p and q are unknown.

| Meals x | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Families f | 6 | p | 10 | q | 4 |

The mean number of meals is 3.

parts.label: (a)

points.description: B1 total frequency: $6 + p + 10 + q + 4 = 40$ gives $p + q = 20$.

parts.explanation: Use the total frequency and the total of fx.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Find the median number of meals.
parts.explanation: The 20th and 21st values: cumulative frequencies 6, 14, 24, so both are 3. Median = 3.
parts.workedSolution: 1. The 20th and 21st values: cumulative frequencies 6, 14, 24, so both are 3. Median = 3.

parts.label: (d)
parts.explanation: x = 4 has the highest frequency, q = 12.
parts.workedSolution: 1. x = 4 has the highest frequency, q = 12.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Compare the mean, median and mode, and comment on the shape of the distribution.

points.description: Mean = median = 3, but mode = 4 is larger.
The data have a longer tail towards small values: slight negative skew.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The mean and median are both 3 and the mode is 4. Since the mode is above the mean and median, the distribution has a longer tail to the left (smaller values): it is slightly negatively skewed.

parts.explanation: For negative skew, mean ≤ median < mode.

explanation: Two equations come from the total frequency and the mean; then use cumulative frequencies for the median and the largest frequency for the mode.
